mainTopic: Which disqualified קרבנות stay on the מזבח once placed there, and which must come down (a ברייתא on ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה״)
overview: This amud brings a ברייתא about a disqualified קרבן that was already put up on the מזבח: must it come down or stay there? It opens in the middle of the first opinion. That opinion uses limiting words in the פסוק to say that three cases must come down: an offering slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, and one whose blood left the קלעים. רבי שמעון disagrees and lists many disqualified offerings, including those same three. He asks where we learn that they stay up. He answers from ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה״: one תורה (one law) covers everything that goes up on the מזבח, so once it is up, it does not come down. He then limits the rule with the word זאת, which leaves out animals that were never fit to be offered, like a טרפה, כלאים, and יוצא דופן. The amud ends with רבי שמעון asking why we include the first group and exclude the second, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three disqualified offerings that must come down
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion in the ברייתא finishes its point. Limiting words in the פסוק exclude three cases: an offering slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, and one whose blood left the קלעים. If any of these went up on the מזבח, it must come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes an offering slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, and one whose blood went outside the curtains. If such an offering went up on the מזבח, it must come down.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle. The first opinion lists three kinds of disqualified offerings that must be taken down from the מזבח even if they were already put up there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that a disqualified offering placed on the מזבח stays there. This opinion reads limiting words in the פסוק as cutting out three cases from that rule. For these three, the rule of staying up does not apply, so they must be taken down.

keyTerms.meaning: Excluding; this cuts out a case from a rule
The curtains around the courtyard of the משכן, meaning the area of the עזרה
Its blood spilled before it could be sprinkled
If it went up onto the מזבח, it must come down

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the start of the discussion. The words ״פרט ל...״ continue a reading of the פסוק that came just before, so these three cases are exceptions to the basic rule that a disqualified offering placed on the מזבח stays there.

phrases.english: Excluding one that was slaughtered at night,
and one whose blood spilled,
and one whose blood went outside the curtains,
so that if it went up, it must come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first opinion's reading of the פסוק from the text just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, or one whose blood left the עזרה must be taken down from the מזבח even if it was already placed there.

steps.title: רבי שמעון begins listing disqualified offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the word עולה by itself only teaches about a valid עולה. He asks where we learn to include a long list of disqualified offerings, among them the very three cases the first opinion excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: from the word 'burnt offering' I only know about a valid burnt offering. From where do we include one slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, one whose blood left the curtains, one left overnight, one taken out, an impure one, leftover meat, and one slaughtered with a plan to eat it outside its time or outside its place?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון opens his own view. He starts a question asking where we learn that many kinds of disqualified offerings also stay on the מזבח once they are up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion. His list includes the same three cases (slaughtered at night, spilled blood, blood taken outside) that the first opinion said must come down. So for him these too stay on the מזבח, and he adds many more cases besides.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know; this means the word by itself teaches just this much
A valid burnt offering
To include; to widen the rule to more cases
Something left overnight past its proper time
Leftover sacrificial meat past its time
Slaughtered while planning to eat or offer it outside its proper time or outside its proper place

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: "burnt offering" —
I only know about a valid burnt offering;
from where do we include one that was slaughtered at night,
and one whose blood spilled,
and one whose blood went outside the curtains,
and that which was left overnight, and that which was taken out,
phrases.notes: Here this means the blood was left overnight, and the offering itself was carried out of the courtyard.

phrases.english: and the impure one, and the leftover,
and one slaughtered intending outside its time or outside its place,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עוֹלָה — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹלָה כְּשֵׁרָה, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a second opinion that includes the very cases the first opinion excluded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source teaches that disqualified offerings, including those slaughtered at night or whose blood spilled or left the עזרה, stay on the מזבח once placed there?

steps.title: More disqualified offerings added to the list
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון keeps adding cases: blood received or sprinkled by people unfit for the service, blood placed in the wrong spot (above or below, inside or outside), and a פסח or חטאת slaughtered for the wrong purpose. He then closes the question: from where?
steps.simpleTranslation: And offerings whose blood unfit people received and sprinkled; blood meant to go above that was put below, or meant for below that was put above; blood meant for outside that was put inside, or meant for inside that was put outside; and a פסח or חטאת slaughtered not for its own purpose. From where do we know these stay up?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his long list and ends with the question "from where?". The גמרא is setting up the answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases are mistakes in how the blood service was done: the wrong person did it, it went in the wrong place, or the wrong purpose was in mind. Every one of them makes the offering disqualified. The question is whether the rule "once up, it stays up" covers even these.

keyTerms.meaning: People unfit to do the Temple service
They sprinkled their blood on the מזבח
Above or below the red line around the middle of the מזבח
The outer מזבח or the inner מזבח inside the היכל
Not for their own sake; slaughtered with a different offering in mind

phrases.english: and those whose blood unfit people received and sprinkled,
and those meant to be placed above that one placed below,
phrases.notes: Above or below the red line around the middle of the מזבח.

phrases.english: and those meant to be placed below that one placed above,
and those meant to be placed outside that one placed inside,
and those meant to be placed inside that one placed outside,
and a Paschal offering and a sin offering that one slaughtered not for their own sake,
from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes רבי שמעון's question that began in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source shows that even offerings with mistakes in the blood service or in their purpose stay on the מזבח once placed there?

steps.title: One law for everything that goes up on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers from ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה״. The word תורה makes one law for everything that goes up on the מזבח: if it went up, it does not come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "This is the law of the burnt offering." It made one law for everything that goes up: if they went up, they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the source for his whole list. The phrase "the law of the עולה" covers every disqualified offering, so none of them come down once they are up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads the word תורה as widening the rule, making one law for everything that goes up on the מזבח, whether valid or not. Because of this, even the three cases the first opinion excluded (slaughtered at night, blood spilled, blood taken outside) stay up in his view. Those three cases are where the two opinions disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; this introduces the source
It included; it widened the rule
One law that covers all the cases
Those things that go up on the מזבח
If they went up, they do not come down

steps.whatToRemember: Basic rule: a disqualified offering that went up on the מזבח stays there. The first opinion takes three cases out of this rule (slaughtered at night, blood spilled, blood taken outside). רבי שמעון keeps even those on the מזבח, learning from ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה״ that there is one law for everything that goes up.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "אם עלו לא ירדו" is the main idea of this ברייתא. In מסכת נדה, it matters because רבי שמעון's list in step 5 includes יוצא דופן, an animal born by caesarean section.

phrases.english: The verse states: "This is the law of the burnt offering" —
it included in one law all things that go up,
that if they went up, they do not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question "from where?" that רבי שמעון asked in steps 2 and 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word תורה in ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה״ makes one law for everything that goes up on the מזבח, so disqualified offerings that went up do not come down.

steps.title: The word זאת excludes animals that were never fit for the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says we might have thought the word תורה also includes animals that are unfit by their very nature, like a רובע, נרבע, מוקצה, נעבד, אתנן, מחיר, כלאים, טרפה, and יוצא דופן. The word זאת teaches that these are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should also include an animal that mated with a person, an animal a person mated with, an animal set aside for idol worship, an animal that was worshipped, an animal given as a prostitute's payment or as the price of a dog, a mixed-breed animal, a טרפה, and an animal born by caesarean section. So the פסוק says 'This' (זאת) to leave them out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון puts a limit on his own wide rule. Some unfit animals are not covered, and the word זאת is what leaves them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תורה brought in a very long list of disqualified offerings. Here רבי שמעון shows that the rule has an edge. The animals in this new list are excluded through the limiting word זאת, so if they went up on the מזבח, they must come down.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that mated with a person, and an animal that a person mated with
An animal set aside for idol worship, and an animal that was itself worshipped as a god
An animal given as payment to a prostitute, and an animal traded for a dog
An animal born from two different species
An animal with a fatal wound or defect
An animal born by caesarean section, literally 'coming out through the wall'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this list up with the earlier one. The cases in steps 2-3 (like blood that spilled or a wrong intention) are included and stay on the מזבח. This new list is excluded and comes down.

phrases.english: One might have thought that I include
phrases.notes: He means: include in the rule 'if it went up, it does not come down.'

phrases.english: an animal that mated with a person, and an animal that a person mated with,
and an animal set aside for idol worship, and an animal that was worshipped,
and a prostitute's payment, and the price of a dog,
and a mixed-breed animal, and a טרפה,
and an animal born by caesarean section?
Therefore the verse says: 'This.'
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק, ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה״. The word 'this' narrows the rule down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the wide inclusion from תורה in step 4 by using the word זאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals that are unfit by nature, such as a רובע, נרבע, מוקצה, נעבד, אתנן, מחיר, כלאים, טרפה, and יוצא דופן, are excluded by זאת. If they went up on the מזבח, they come down.

steps.title: Why include one group and exclude the other?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks what reason we have for including the first list of disqualified offerings and excluding the second list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you include these cases and exclude those cases?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון asks for the reason behind the split between the two lists. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists are made up of offerings that cannot be brought. So we need a reason why תורה goes with the first list and זאת goes with the second. The question asks for the principle that tells the two groups apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see, meaning: what is your reason?
To include in the rule
To exclude from the rule

phrases.english: And what did you see,
phrases.notes: In plain words: what is your reason?

phrases.english: to include these
phrases.notes: 'These' are the disqualified offerings from steps 2-3, which stay on the מזבח.

phrases.english: and to exclude those?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת אֵלּוּ וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the line drawn in step 5 between included and excluded cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that separates offerings that stay on the מזבח (included by תורה) from those that come down (excluded by זאת).
